about: Review histories and the card py-fsrs derives from them. Fold each case's events ordered by (reviewed_at, event_id), counting a repeated event_id once, starting from an empty card, and compare with `expected` (and `after_each`, one entry per distinct event in fold order). due_ms and last_review_ms are epoch milliseconds; stability and difficulty are exact doubles.

cases.name: six_good_on_due
cases.note: Good every time, each review exactly when due.

cases.name: mixed_with_lapse
cases.note: Good, Hard, Good, Again at due, then relearn.

cases.name: again_then_good
cases.note: Again on a new card, then Good.

cases.name: easy_three_times
cases.note: Easy on a new card, repeated on due.

cases.name: hard_at_first_step
cases.note: Hard keeps a new card on its first learning step.

cases.name: same_day_burst
cases.note: Several reviews inside one day, then a long gap.

cases.name: late_review
cases.note: A review 20 days after it was due.

cases.name: relearning_steps
cases.note: Lapse a graduated card, then walk its relearning step.

cases.name: ends_mid_learning
cases.note: A new card rated Good once: still Learning, on step 1.

cases.name: ends_in_relearning
cases.note: A graduated card that lapses on the last event.

cases.name: tied_timestamps
cases.note: Two events with the same timestamp fold in event_id order.

cases.name: listed_out_of_order
cases.note: The events are listed out of order; the fold sorts them.

cases.name: duplicate_delivery
cases.note: One event delivered twice counts once.

cases.name: forty_reviews
cases.note: A seeded history of 40 reviews, early and late.
